title: ProspectAI: try it for free
author: Downtown_Extension_6
selftext:
I built a 6-agent AI pipeline for stock research — here's how it works and 4 picks from its first month

Disclosure: [ProspectAI](https://prospect-ai.moisesprat.dev) is my own project, sharing it here since this sub is for AI-investment tools.

**What it is**: a multi-agent pipeline (built on CrewAI) that researches a stock portfolio end to end. Six specialized agents run in sequence:

1. Market analyst— macro/sector context    
2. Technical analyst — price structure, momentum    
3. Fundamental analyst — valuation, financials    
4. Draft strategist — assembles a candidate portfolio + trade setups    
5. Adversarial Critic — its only job is to attack the draft: overlooked risks, contradictory signals, weak theses    
6. Final strategist — revises based on the critique

The design principle: **LLMs reason, deterministic tools calculate**. The agents decide which signals matter; every number (scores, allocations, entry/exit math) is computed in Python, never by the model. Agents pass typed Pydantic objects, not freeform text, so one agent can't quietly reinterpret another's output. Runs stream live to the browser over SSE.

**Some hits from the first month**: entry → today, marked-to-market Jun 26):

MU— semis call, +56%    
WDC — +22%    
LLY — healthcare, +25%    
GRC — industrials, +23%

The honest part, because it matters: across all 66 signals it averaged +4.75%, with +6.2pp alpha vs SPY (65% beat rate). BUT against equal-weight RSP the edge drops to +1.5pp (58% beat) — because over these windows cap-weighted SPY fell while equal-weight rose. So a lot of the SPY alpha is sector allocation (avoiding mega-cap tech), not pure stock selection. Equal-weight is the fairer benchmark, and on that the edge is real but modest. It's paper-traded, positions still open, single \\\~6-week regime — not a track record yet.

Happy to get into the agent architecture, the critic's failure-mode checklist, or how the deterministic/LLM boundary works.

comments.author: Must_Dragonfruit
comments.body:
probably smart to make this an agentic stack... 

but this is pretty basic stuff...

I don't understand why you'd let an LLM pick the stocks. There's no way to know whether there's a bias in its training.

replies.author: Downtown_Extension_6
replies.body:
Thank you for your feedback; it’s a very valid concern. Let me explain how the system is built so you can see that the model’s stock selection won’t be biased by its training data.

At ProspectAI, there’s a clear separation between tasks that can be handled by LLMs like reasoning and report generation and those that need to be done deterministically. When a Market Analyst selects candidate stocks, the LLM is simply used to calibrate sentiment analysis – a task where the model excels – and the pure selection logic resides in deterministic code (scores, ranking and allocation).  Furthermore, tools are used to crawl Reddit posts and identify stock candidates – this is also outside the LLM’s capabilities.

This separation helps minimise bias stemming from training data.

I hope this helps!
